correctness.rationale: Every 5-bit binary de Bruijn cycle corresponds uniquely to one feedback function f(x0,t)=x0 XOR g(t) with g on all 16 possible four-bit states. Enumerating all 65536 g, accepting only 32-state Hamiltonian returns to 00000, exhausts rotation classes without duplicates. Circular discrepancy equals the range of 33 integer prefix sums because the period contains 16 of each symbol. Direct canonical rotation tests of c/r/cr yield all 2048 counts, conditional 64 CR counts and orbit-size distribution. A completely separate anti-palindromic 16-bit halfword census tests all 65536 X and independently finds 128 valid halfwords, 64 distinct rotation classes and conditional 16/16/24/8. Mathematical coverage arguments, not finite sampling assumptions, make computation a complete finite proof.

value.rationale: Circular symbol discrepancy affects balance and spectral concentration, while CR symmetry defines a recognized constrained de Bruijn family. This supplies the exact complete interaction at the first nontrivial odd order where the two constraints vary: all CR frequencies, optimal-within-symmetry fraction and every complement/reversal orbit size, including previously unreported nonoptimal strata. Natural finite classification is motivated without claiming a higher-order general theorem. The D=6..8 cells distinguish symmetry-conditioned design options not implied by general existence or marginal counts.
